name: Lofty
tagline: Buy and sell fractional shares of rental properties on an exchange, with rent and governance attached

pricing.notes: No subscription, no management fee, no profit share. Buyers pay 2.5-3% and sellers pay 3-3.5% per trade. No minimum investment since fractional share investing launched.
pricing.freeTier: Browsing properties and opening an account are free; fees apply only when a share trades.

verdictSummary: The software is real work (a marketplace frontend, a backend, and smart contracts moving share balances on a blockchain) and an agent can still rebuild all of it. The prompt below does the local version. What it cannot rebuild is everything around the code: the two-sided market of buyers and sellers already trading, the legal structure that keeps the shares as LLC membership interests instead of registered securities because owners actively govern the assets, and the community that votes on property decisions and talks to sellers. A clone launches empty, and recreating that legal structure is a law-firm project, not a coding project.
coreLoopDIY: Simulate a fractional property exchange: seed properties and owners, trade shares through an order book, accrue rent to share balances, and run per-property governance votes weighted by shares.
whatYouLose: liquidity: the buyers and sellers already trading, which is the product
the legal structure that keeps shares tradable as LLC interests instead of registered securities
real properties: sourcing, diligence, and onboarding houses people actually want
rent operations: collecting from tenants and paying out to hundreds of owners
the governance community: owners who vote on decisions and talk to sellers
moatNotes: two-sided liquidity plus a governance structure that keeps the shares out of securities territory; the owner community is the retention
replacementScope: local simulation of the mechanics for learning or demos
ongoingBurden: property sourcing, rent collection, payouts, order matching, governance administration, and every legal question the structure answers
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody pays Lofty for its frontend. Buyers pay 2.5-3% per trade because that is where the sellers, the properties, and the rent already are, and sellers pay 3-3.5% because that is where the buyers are. Owners are not passive investors: they vote with their shares on what happens to each property and talk to sellers in the community tab. The fee buys a working market and a legal structure, not an interface.

notes: Self-submitted by the operator. Fee ranges, the no-minimum change, and the governance structure confirmed directly by the team on 2026-09-02.
prompt:
Build me a local simulation of a fractional real-estate exchange like Lofty, for learning and demos. Requirements:

- Node.js, Express, better-sqlite3, server-rendered pages with vanilla JS, no frontend framework, one process.
- Seed 6 rental properties with a name, address, photo URL, share supply, share price, and monthly rent, plus 8 bot owners with starting cash and share balances.
- The core loop: place limit buy and sell orders per property; matching orders trade, move shares and cash between balances, and record every fill in a trades table.
- A rent job: every day at midnight, credit each owner property_rent * shares_held / share_supply / 30, and show a per-owner rent ledger page.
- A governance page per property: any owner holding shares can open a proposal (one-line title plus description) and owners vote yes or no weighted by shares; a proposal closes after 7 days or when one side passes 50% of outstanding shares.
- Interface: a local web page on port 3000 showing the property grid, each order book, my portfolio, and open proposals; a dropdown switches which seeded owner I act as.
- No accounts, no passwords, no telemetry, no real money, no blockchain: balances live in SQLite and the README says so.
- Out of scope: real tokens, payments, and KYC. The real product cannot legally operate without them, and standing them up is legal and vendor work, not code an agent one-shots. This simulates the mechanics, which is the part that is easy.
- README with setup, the matching and rent math, and how to reseed the database.
